PhD thesis, Ball State University (ix + 223 leaves; advisor Herbert Stahlke); author's abstract on the Ball State Cardinal Scholar record hdl:20.500.14291/174922 (published version: Baloubi, Desire 2005, same title, Charlotte NC: Conquering Books). Corroboration: Kluge, Angela (2011). A sociolinguistic survey of the Ede language communities of Benin and Togo, Volume 4: Idaca language area. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2011-005, 39 pp.
catalog_locator: Baloubi 2000: dc.description.abstract of the Cardinal Scholar record (https://cardinalscholar.bsu.edu/handle/20.500.14291/174922;thesis body not deposited). Kluge 2011 vol. 4: sec. 5.1.1 'Internal comprehension', p. 12, repeated in the summary p. 21.
catalog_quote: [Baloubi 2000, author's abstract:] Particular attention is paid to vowel harmony (VH) and tones. ... In regard to tones, it is pointed out that a three-way tonal system is a major characteristic of the language. However, a phenomenon of M/L neutralization is underlined in a specific environment: a final low tone in a verb followed by a direct object noun. In this environment, a low (L) tone changes to mid (M) ... like Standard Yoruba (SY), Idaacha has open syllables: V and CV. [Kluge 2011 vol. 4, p. 12] Linguistic differences between the different Idaca villages throughout the area are reportedly minor and mainly phonological or at the level of tone

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Not a stress statement, but for the record: Kluge 2011 Vol 4 (Idaca language area, SIL ESR 2011-005), p. 17 (sec. 5.1.1 Internal comprehension) and p. 26 (summary): 'Linguistic differences between the different Idaca villages throughout the area are reportedly minor and mainly phonological or at the level of tone, without bringing about a semantic change.' This presupposes Idaca is tonal (consistent with Baloubi's three-way system) but says nothing about stress. Intro+Vol 1, Appendix K note 36 (p. 93): 'Tone markings were transcribed but were not included in the analysis due to ambiguities in proper weighting.' No stress content in either volume.

Série électronique de documents de travail, SIL Togo-Bénin, numéro 12. 18 pp. SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 86507 (date created 2017, issued 2020).
sources.note: Report (oral communication to Idaasha literacy workers and translators, Dassa-Zoumé, 21 July 2017) of a quantitative literacy experiment (Dassa-Zoumé, 23-24 June 2015) testing how far full ('intégrale') representation of tone in the Idaasha orthography contributes to oral reading fluency, comprehension and spelling accuracy; presupposes and very likely summarises the Idaasha lexical tone system and its tone-marking conventions (the on-file abstract of Baloubi 2000 gives a three-way H/M/L system); number of tones not stated in the abstract.
